newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian parliament's budget timetable amended. [CORRECTED 11:07 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Italian parliament's budget timetable amended. [CORRECTED 11:07 GMT]

text.p: The timetable for examination of Italy's 1997 budget in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) has been amended though the end of debate in the full assembly will remain November 17, parliamentary sources said on Thursday. (Corrects from "though the start of the debate..." to make clear that lower house has until November 17 to conclude budget debate.)
They said the budget commission in the lower house would have until October 28 to examine the budget. The initial deadline for approval by the commission was October 26.

Other commissions of the lower house, which will examine aspects of the budget relating to their areas of legislation, will have until October 15 to express an opinion, rather than October 13, the sources said.
The timetable amendments were agreed at a meeting of parliamentary party leaders.

The budget aims to reduce the 1997 deficit by 62.5 trillion lire and allow Italy to qualify for Europe's single currency. It must go to the Senate after passage through the Chamber and has to be approved by the end of the year.
